description: The scan Mode itself: the continuous neck-tracker + concurrent arm-only responder loop, weighted dispatch, person vs person+dog placeholder logging, CLI --action=scan branch and --scan-timeout-min flag in animatronic.py, and the web control-panel toggle/routes/launcher/timeout-persistence in webapp.py (+ template). Depends on FEAT-001 (rest_channels, config_store timeout accessors) and FEAT-002 (allowlist, choose_scan_action, scan_rules, arm-only brains/hypnotic builders).
steps: In src/animatronic.py import ARM_ONLY_CHANNELS, SCAN_GESTURE_CHANNELS, SCAN_SAFE_ARM_ACTIONS, ScanActionKind, choose_scan_action, scan_rules, DEFAULT_DOG_LABEL from detection_routine_map (alongside the existing DetectionRoutineMap import).

Add Animatronic.scan(self, camera_url=DEFAULT_CAMERA_URL, timeout_seconds=None, ...tracking tuning kwargs mirroring tracking()...) modelled on tracking(): build TrackingConfig, CameraClient, routine_map=DetectionRoutineMap(scan_rules()); build the scan_responses map binding each ENABLED allowlist name to its arm-only callable using one shared Movements instance mv: 'beckon': lambda: mv.beckon(), 'comeHere': lambda: mv.come_here(), 'wave': lambda: mv._wave_arm(include_neck=False), 'brains': lambda: self._run_scan_performance(self._brains_performance(scan=True)), 'hypnotic': lambda: self._run_scan_performance(self._hypnotic_performance(scan=True)). Keep SCAN_SAFE_ARM_ACTIONS and scan_responses in lockstep (burp commented out in both). Clear nap_signal on entry, compute a monotonic deadline from timeout_seconds, run asyncio.run(self._run_scan_loop(...)), recenter the neck in an except backstop, and clear nap_signal on exit. scan() takes NO lock itself.

Add async Animatronic._run_scan_loop(self, client, cfg, routine_map, scan_responses, mv, deadline): a continuous neck tracker owning channels 0-1 (reuse get_detections/select_target/compute_offset/next_neck_targets and set_angle on NECK_PAN/NECK_TILT exactly like _run_tracking_loop, and reuse _run_scan_sweep VERBATIM when no target). The tracker NEVER winds down to run a response. Track the in-flight response as self._active = (task, rule). Each iteration after rule = routine_map.select_action(dets, time.monotonic()): if self._active is None and rule is not None -> if DEFAULT_DOG_LABEL in rule.required_classes: print('[scan] person+dog detected (walkYourDog placeholder)'); name = choose_scan_action(); dispatch via the guarded helper (next step) as self._active = (asyncio.create_task(self._dispatch_scan_response(name, scan_responses, mv)), rule). elif self._active is not None and self._active[0].done(): task, fired_rule = self._active; self._active = None; try: task.result() except Exception as e: print('[scan] response failed: '+str(e)); routine_map.mark_completed(fired_rule, time.monotonic()). Poll done() — never await the response task in the loop. Break on nap_signal.stop_requested() at the top of each iteration OR when time.monotonic() >= deadline (print '[scan] timeout -> wound down'). finally (strict order): (1) if self._active is not None: self._active[0].cancel(); await asyncio.gather(self._active[0], return_exceptions=True); (2) self._recenter_neck(tilt_angle=cfg.tilt_center_deg); (3) return.

Add async Animatronic._dispatch_scan_response(self, name, scan_responses, mv): membership-guard name in scan_responses (log+return if absent). For a Gesture (SCAN_SAFE_ARM_ACTIONS[name] is ScanActionKind.GESTURE) assert SCAN_GESTURE_CHANNELS.get(name) is not None and SCAN_GESTURE_CHANNELS[name] <= ARM_ONLY_CHANNELS; on miss/absent, print and return (fail-closed, never crash the loop). Then try: await scan_responses[name]() except Exception: for a Gesture that may have died before lowering, best-effort await Movements.trunkController.return_to_rest(channels=ARM_ONLY_CHANNELS) and re-raise so the loop logs it. (Performance responses rest the arm themselves via FEAT-001 rest_channels.)

Add Animatronic._run_scan_performance(self, defn): construct PerformanceRunner(defn, mv_or_self_mv, self._resolve_audio_dir(), rest_channels=ARM_ONLY_CHANNELS) and await .run() inside the loop's running event loop (do NOT call asyncio.run here — _run_scan_loop already runs under asyncio.run). Use the same shared Movements instance the scan_responses lambdas use.

In src/animatronic.py main() add 'scan' to build_action_map() for allowlist parity only, then add an 'elif args.action == 'scan':' branch placed BEFORE the generic 'elif args.action in action_map:' branch (so it shadows the generic one). The branch wraps the call in 'with servo_lock():' and calls a.scan(camera_url=args.camera_url, timeout_seconds=max(1, min(120, args.scan_timeout_min)) * 60, ...optional tuning kwargs...). On ServoBusyError print the busy message and sys.exit(BUSY_EXIT_CODE).

In the argparse block add parser.add_argument('--scan-timeout-min', dest='scan_timeout_min', type=int, default=60, help='Scan mode: minutes before the timeout winds the mode down, clamped 1-120 (default 60). Only used with --action=scan.'). Keep it DISTINCT from the existing --scan-timeout (the tracking reacquire timeout in seconds).

In src/webapp.py add SCAN_ACTIONS = {'scan'} near TRACKING_ACTIONS. Add run_scan(timeout_min) mirroring run_tracking: cmd = [VENV_PYTHON, ANIMATRONIC, '--action=scan', f'--scan-timeout-min={int(timeout_min)}']; nap_signal.clear_stop(); return subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=PROJECT_DIR). All argv entries fixed/validated — never shell-interpolated.

In src/webapp.py add launch_scan(timeout_min) mirroring launch_napping/launch_awake: under _launch_lock, if _mic_is_streaming() and not _stop_mic(): return False, busy message (scan owns the jaw/audio path); if _gesture_busy(): return False busy; proc = run_scan(timeout_min); set _active_proc proc/label='scan', _last_action; return True, message. No watchdog (open-ended Mode).

In src/webapp.py add @app.route('/scan/<state>', methods=['POST']) def scan(state): on 'start' gate 'scan' in SCAN_ACTIONS; read minutes from request.json (key e.g. 'timeout_min'); if provided, require int and 1<=n<=120 else return 400 (reject non-int AND out-of-range, stricter than /tracking); if omitted, n = config_store.load_scan_timeout(); persist via config_store.save_scan_timeout(n); ok,msg = launch_scan(n); 409 on busy else success. On 'stop' call nap_signal.request_stop() and return success. Unknown state -> 400.
In src/webapp.py add 'scan' to _MODE_LABELS so a later web action preempts a running scan via _preempt_mode_if_running.

Add a scan control-panel button + a minutes number input (min=1 max=120 default=60) to the Flask control-panel template under src/templates/, mirroring the existing tracking/awake controls and POSTing to /scan/start and /scan/stop.

Add tests/test_scan_loop.py (SERVO_SIM convention) with a fake detections source and stubbed response callables: assert the neck tracker keeps issuing NECK_PAN/NECK_TILT writes across a response; only ONE response is in flight at a time; the responder prints the person+dog placeholder line when the dog label is present and dispatches choose_scan_action() (not rule.action); the Gesture subset guard logs-and-skips a non-subset or missing name (fail-closed); and a cancelled in-flight task is awaited during wind-down before _recenter_neck.

Add web route tests (extend tests/test_proxies.py or add tests/test_scan_routes.py) with Flask's test client and subprocess spawning / _stop_mic monkeypatched: POST /scan/start persists a valid minutes value (temp config) and returns success; non-int and out-of-range (0, 121) return 400 and launch nothing; omitting the value reads persisted/default 60; POST /scan/stop calls nap_signal.request_stop(); 'scan' is in SCAN_ACTIONS and _MODE_LABELS; launch_scan attempts _stop_mic().
acceptance_criteria: The neck tracker keeps stepping across a response and only one response runs at a time; the person+dog placeholder line is logged and a weighted (not rule.action) choice is dispatched; the Gesture subset guard fails closed; verified by passing tests/test_scan_loop.py.

POST /scan/start persists the timeout and rejects non-int/out-of-range with 400; /scan/stop requests a stop; 'scan' is in SCAN_ACTIONS and _MODE_LABELS; launch_scan stops the mic; verified by passing web route tests.
main() dispatches --action=scan via the dedicated branch BEFORE the generic branch under a single servo_lock(); --scan-timeout-min is distinct from --scan-timeout.

Safety preserved: all neck/arm writes go through set_angle/move_to; every response rests the arm (Performance via rest_channels=ARM_ONLY_CHANNELS, gesture via its own lower or the fail path); wind-down cancels+awaits the in-flight task then recenters; no double servo_lock acquisition.

findings: IMPLEMENTED. src/animatronic.py: imports now pull ARM_ONLY_CHANNELS, SCAN_GESTURE_CHANNELS, SCAN_SAFE_ARM_ACTIONS, ScanActionKind, choose_scan_action, scan_rules, DEFAULT_DOG_LABEL from detection_routine_map. New Animatronic methods (placed after _recenter_neck, before build_action_map): scan(camera_url, timeout_seconds=None, +TrackingConfig tuning kwargs) — builds TrackingConfig like tracking(), DetectionRoutineMap(scan_rules()), one shared Movements mv, and the scan_responses map {'beckon': mv.beckon(), 'comeHere': mv.come_here(), 'wave': mv._wave_arm(include_neck=False), 'brains'/'hypnotic': self._run_scan_performance(self._<name>_performance(mv, scan=True), mv)} (burp commented out in both scan_responses and SCAN_SAFE_ARM_ACTIONS). scan() clears nap_signal on entry, computes a monotonic deadline (None => no timeout), runs asyncio.run(_run_scan_loop(...)), recenters neck in an except backstop, clears nap_signal in finally, and takes NO lock itself. async _run_scan_loop(client, cfg, routine_map, scan_responses, mv, deadline) — neck tracker owning channels 0/1 reusing get_detections/select_target/compute_offset/next_neck_targets + set_angle, reusing _run_scan_sweep VERBATIM when no target (scan NEVER ends on a sweep timeout, it just continues; only nap_signal/deadline end it). self._active=(task,rule) is the single in-flight response; dispatch only when self._active is None and rule is not None; polls task.done() (never awaits in the loop); on done -> task.result() (log on exception) + routine_map.mark_completed(rule, now). person+dog logged via 'DEFAULT_DOG_LABEL in rule.required_classes' and ALWAYS dispatches choose_scan_action() (weighted, not rule.action). finally (strict order): cancel+await self._active[0] via asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True), then _recenter_neck(tilt_angle=cfg.tilt_center_deg). async _dispatch_scan_response(name, scan_responses, mv) — membership-guard name in scan_responses (log+return); for a GESTURE assert SCAN_GESTURE_CHANNELS.get(name) is not None and <= ARM_ONLY_CHANNELS (fail-closed log+return on miss); await the callable; on exception a GESTURE best-effort awaits Movements.trunkController.return_to_rest(channels=ARM_ONLY_CHANNELS) then re-raises (Performances rest themselves via rest_channels). _run_scan_performance(defn, mv) RETURNS the PerformanceRunner(defn, mv, self._resolve_audio_dir(), ambient=<hypnotic blink only>, rest_channels=ARM_ONLY_CHANNELS).run() COROUTINE (no asyncio.run — _run_scan_loop already runs under asyncio.run). NOTE: the perf builders take (self, mv, scan=...) per FEAT-002 (not (self, scan=...) as the step text abbreviated) — _run_scan_performance is called with the already-built defn. build_action_map() gained 'scan': self.scan for allowlist parity. main() gained an 'elif args.action == 'scan':' branch placed BEFORE the generic 'elif args.action in action_map:' branch; SCAN_ACTIONS={'scan'}; run_scan(timeout_min) mirroring run_tracking (fixed argv [VENV_PYTHON, ANIMATRONIC, '--action=scan', f'--scan-timeout-min={int(timeout_min)}'], nap_signal.clear_stop(), Popen cwd=PROJECT_DIR); launch_scan(timeout_min) mirroring launch_napping (under _launch_lock: auto-_stop_mic since scan owns jaw/audio, _gesture_busy guard, run_scan, set _active_proc label='scan', no watchdog); @app.route('/scan/<state>') scan(state) — 'start' gates 'scan' in SCAN_ACTIONS, reads request.json 'timeout_min': if provided require a real int (bool rejected) in [1,120] else 400 (stricter than /tracking — rejects both non-int AND out-of-range), if omitted uses config_store.load_scan_timeout();
